full_text: Intro What is an Assumable Mortgage? Understanding the Process, Pros and Cons Home » What is an Assumable Mortgage? Understanding the Process, Pros and Cons Are you rethinking your plans to buy a home because of increasing interest rates? You are not alone; there are many other people who also feel like they are stuck in a situation of uncertainty due to rising interest rates and have questions about whether or not they can afford to purchase a home today. However, there are different ways to get around the high interest rates and still purchase a home as long as you know about assumable mortgages! An assumable mortgage is beneficial for buyers as it may result in lower monthly payments than would be required with a new loan. Buyers find it easier to qualify for the mortgage since they are taking over an existing loan from the previous homeowner. Sellers can benefit from an assumable mortgage as it may add to the appeal of their property in a competitive environment and may lead to a quicker sale. So, assumable mortgage benefits cannot be denied. This blog will provide details about what an assumable mortgage is, the assumable mortgage process and the advantages and disadvantages of using an assumable mortgage. Understanding Assumable Mortgages When purchasing a home, one of your options is to assume an existing mortgage. It allows you (the buyer) to continue making payments on the seller’s current mortgage. Assuming an existing mortgage can provide great savings if current market interest rates are higher than the interest rate on the seller’s mortgage. It is important to note that not all mortgages are assumable. An FHA mortgage or a VA mortgage are typically assumable mortgages with the lender’s permission. Many conventional mortgages have more stringent requirements to be converted to an assumable mortgage. Before deciding to assume an existing mortgage, you should be well versed in the type of mortgage or assumable mortgage requirements. Moreover, it is mandatory to know the mortgage assumption process for lenders in detail. How Does An Assumed Mortgage Work? A typical mortgage assumption process for lender has the following steps: Application Process – The buyer submits an assumption request to the lender. Lender Approval – The lender reviews the buyer’s credit history, income, and financial situation. Transfer of Obligation – If the lender approves the buyer, he/she (the buyer) assumes the seller’s obligations and makes the mortgage payments. Who Can Use an Assumable Mortgage? Assumable Mortgages can benefit: A buyer is an ideal candidate for assuming an existing mortgage since they can save money if interest rates rise, and they also have the ability to lock into a lower rate. Sellers will find their home more appealing to potential buyers in the current competitive market if they accept an assumable mortgage. Historical Context & Market Trends Loan servicing and mortgage assumption have been around for many years, and they have mainly been FHA and VA loans. However, with the increase in mortgage interest rates, more buyers and sellers are interested in assumable mortgages as a great alternative due to the savings it will provide. Types of Assumable Mortgages FHA Loans FHA mortgages are guaranteed by the FHA. The advantages for buyers of assuming an FHA loan include a low down payment (which can be as little as 3.5%) and more lenient credit approvals. Pros: Lower initial costs, more relaxed qualification standards, and the opportunity to assume a low-interest rate loan. Cons: Monthly mortgage insurance premium payments are required along with the monthly mortgage payment. VA Loans Eligible veterans, active-duty service members and certain surviving spouses can use VA loans. However, if a Veteran grants a non-veteran to assume their loan, the Veteran’s VA right remains attached to that house until the loan is paid off. The primary benefit of a VA loan allows another qualified buyer to take over the loan from the original borrower. The new buyer can assume the current loan from the seller which requires no substantial down payment as long as they fulfill the lender’s standards. Pros: No private mortgage insurance; reasonably priced interest rates; easy to assume if making sure that you meet all requirements for assuming loan. Cons: A VA funding fee may apply in certain cases. Conventional Mortgages Conventional mortgages are rarely assumable unless specifically allowed in the loan agreement. USDA loans, however, are generally assumable with lender approval. Cons: Higher barriers for approval, may be required to pay the difference between home value and the remaining balance of the loan, and often includes a due-on-sale clause, making assumption uncommon. Pros: May be able to assume a lower interest rate than is currently in effect for new loans. Feature FHA Loan VA Loan Conventional Loan Down Payment As low as 3.5% Often 0% Usually 5% - 20% Interest Rate Fixed Fixed Fixed or adjustable Assumable? Yes with lender’s approval Yes with lender’s approval Rarely Approval Process Moderate review Moderate review Strict review Mortgage Insurance Required Not required May require PMI if less than 20% Funding Fee None VA funding fee may apply None Best For Buyers with low credit Eligible veterans and service members Buyers seeking conventional financing Main Advantage Easier qualification, low down payment No PMI, strong veteran benefits Potential lower rate Main Drawback Ongoing mortgage insurance Possible funding fee Not easy to assume Step-by-Step Process to Assume a Mortgage Preliminary Steps Look at the interest rate, loan balance and remaining term of the seller’s mortgage. Also, you should familiarize yourself with the lender’s requirements for assuming the mortgage as well as any restrictions on eligibility for assumptors. Application Process You will need to complete and submit an application to the lender to assume the existing obligation. Your application will contain your credit history (with FICO scores), proof of income, assets and liabilities. Approval and Transfer After the lender approves the assumption, the involved parties enter into a loan assumption contract that outlines the current loan balance, monthly payment amount, as well as specified changes. Post-Transfer Considerations The buyer will also assume complete responsibility for making monthly mortgage payments after the loan has been transferred, managing escrow accounts, and fulfilling all other obligations related to the mortgage loan. If the lender accepts the assumption, the buyer will then take complete responsibility for making the monthly payment, managing the escrow account, and abiding by all loan terms. It is extremely important for you to be organized to prevent late payments and/or penalties. The majority of borrowers use some type of digital tools or loan management software to keep track of their mortgage payments and to facilitate the proper management of their mortgages. Example Scenario If you have a mortgage for $300,000 at a 4% interest rate, which has now increased by 2% to 6%, you will save thousands of dollars in interest during the life of the loan, if you are allowed to assume your friend’s loan. Once you have completed lender approval, paid an assumption fee, and assumed the monthly mortgage payments at the original 4%, you will be able to benefit more than if you were to apply for a new mortgage. Pros and Cons of Assumable Mortgages Assumable Mortgage Benefits: Lower Interest Rates Buyers who assume an existing mortgage may benefit from established loan terms that could be more favorable than newly issued mortgages. Reduced Closing Costs Generally speaking, assuming an existing mortgage involves less fees and less costly closing costs than taking out a brand-new loan. Faster Loan Approval Since the loan is already in existence, lenders are usually much more concerned about how creditworthy and financially stable the buyer is. The approval process may be streamlined compared to originating a brand-new loan. Attractive Option for Sellers When you promote your property, you can indicate that it will allow the buyer to get the benefit of a current lower-rate mortgage. This feature could help sell your home faster and differentiate your property from other listings in a highly-competitive market. Start with Existing Equity Position A buyer who is taking over an existing mortgage will receive credit for the amount of payment made toward the principal since the seller originated the loan. Assumable mortgages can create mutual benefits for both buyers and sellers when structured properly. The purchaser will benefit by saving on interest, experiencing lower costs, and obtaining an equity position in the home from day one. Assumable Mortgage Drawbacks: Qualification Requirements The lender will review the buyer’s financial profile to confirm they are capable of managing the remaining loan balance. Limited Availability Other than FHA (Federal Housing Authority) or VA (Veterans Administration) insured loans there aren’t many other types of Loans available for Assumption. Potential Hidden Costs Purchasing a property via an Assumption of Mortgage may not be the least money you will pay to purchase the Property. Moreover, there can be closing costs and prepayments costs too. Liability Issues for Sellers Sellers must confirm that legal responsibility is fully transferred to avoid future financial exposure if payments are missed. Market Risk Additionally, the interest rates may fluctuate. Should an interest rate decrease after a mortgage is assumed, the buyer would miss an opportunity to obtain an even better interest rate if he/she had taken out a new loan. Cost Considerations (Assumable Mortgage Rates) Assumption Fees Assuming a mortgage typically involves an assumption fee charged by most lenders for transferring the mortgage from seller to buyer. Most fees can range between $500 to $1000 and include the administrative fee. In general, fees charged to assume a VA loan may be higher, since the VA allows the lender to charge for a “reasonable” processing fee plus 0.5% of the loan balance (but this will not apply if the buyer is exempt due to a service-connected disability). Down Payment Requirements Depending on whether the purchase price of the home being sold is greater than the balance of the mortgage loan, a down payment may be required even if you are assuming an existing mortgage. Closing Costs The buyer should budget for escrow, title, recording fees, and other incidental costs. The cost of these items may vary from lender to lender and from location to location. Impact on Taxes Buyers who assume a mortgage may be able to benefit from a mortgage interest deduction on their taxes. In addition, the seller will need to determine how the sale of the property will impact their property taxes and possible capital gains. Strategic Considerations for Buyers and Sellers When Buyers Should Consider an Assumable Mortgage? For buyers with excellent credit, lenders generally approve of the mortgage assumption process. Additionally, a buyer may benefit from taking over an existing mortgage because it will give them a lower amount of cash needed for a down payment. Exploring options such as custom mortgage development can also help buyers compare personalized loan structures against an assumable mortgage to determine which strategy offers the greatest long-term advantage. When Sellers Should Encourage Assumption? Mortgage assumption can help sellers to sell their homes more quickly. By providing an assumable loan as part of the sale, the seller is giving the buyer a reason to purchase their property, as most buyers find it appealing. Offering an assumable mortgage may also help sellers to generate a greater level of interest from buyers. Lastly, if the seller receives a full release of liability from the lender, they will lessen their exposure/risk if the buyer defaults on their mortgage obligations later. The FHA and VA loan system requires lenders to free sellers from their obligations when buyers meet credit standards and assume their responsibilities after receiving official approval. The process for handling existing loans which originated before 1980 has developed into a standardized procedure used in present-day operations. Tips for Smooth Assumption Transactions Proper planning is essential for a successful assumable mortgage transaction. It is important for both buyer and seller to work with professional real estate agents who are knowledgeable about the process. In addition, contacting mortgage lenders early in the transaction will ensure that the necessary documents are completed and provide an understanding of what will be acceptable to mortgage lenders. An attorney may also be needed to review the sales contracts in order to assist the buyer and seller in avoiding common pitfalls. Alternatives to Assumable Mortgages Traditional mortgage financing: Conventional financing is the most common alternative. Buyers will usually need to find and apply for a new loan with a mortgage lender. There are many different loan products to choose from when selecting a lender including fixed-rate, adjustable-rate, and interest-only loans with competitive interest rates. Seller financing options: Certain sellers will use seller financing. This makes it easier for buyers who don’t have much credit or money. You make your payments directly to the seller instead of the bank. However, since the seller is lending, there may be a higher interest rate, and more risk if the buyer does not pay. FHA/VA refinancing: If a buyer currently has an FHA or VA loan on their home, they may want to re-finance through these programs rather than assume the mortgage of the seller. This may allow the buyer to get a better interest rate and have government-backed protections available. HELOC or home equity loans: Buyers who already own a home and have some equity may consider using their current home’s equity to help finance their purchase of a new home. Home equity lines of credit (also known as a HELOC) or home equity loans are two ways buyers can get access to funds needed to purchase a new home. Wrapping Up Loan servicing and mortgage assumption go hand in hand. A buyer may be able to save money from the assumed mortgage and incur lower upfront costs, as well as receive a quicker loan approval. A seller could also find that marketing his or her property with an assumable mortgage adds to the appeal of the home. Therefore, it may sell more quickly, resulting in reduced risk to the seller if the lender properly releases the liability from the property. The buyer must qualify with the current loan servicer against the property that he or she wants to buy, and must also prepare to pay certain fees. To properly plan for an assumable mortgage transaction, both buyers and sellers can rely on their real estate agents, lenders, and legal advisers to ensure a smooth transaction. In markets characterized by high-interest rates, savvy buyers who do not have considerable cash reserves and/or sellers can benefit from taking advantage of assumable mortgages. Although each situation may not be appropriate for an assumable mortgage, when approached correctly, these transactions can produce substantial financial rewards. So, would you like to take advantage of an assumable mortgage for your next purchase? Contact us today to determine if you qualify and lock in lower rates before market conditions change! FAQs 1. Can anyone assume an FHA or VA loan? It depends on the lenders. They will consider a few factors before such as: Credit history Financial stability Payment to be made 2. Are conventional loans typically assumable? No, they are not. Most contain a due-on-sale clause, this gives the lender the legal right to demand the full balance if the title transfers. 3. How do I know if I qualify to assume a mortgage? Consider the following: Obtain lender’s approval Income Debt to income ratio Need of financial document Pre-approval 4. What fees are associated with assuming a mortgage? Most assumption fees range between $500 – $1,000. Depending on loan documents, there may also be pre-payment penalties or other expenses related to the assumption. 5. Does the seller remain liable after the mortgage is assumed? It is possible but it depends on the lender. In case, the lender doesn’t release the seller from the debt, the seller will remain liable until a formal written release is received. 6. Can an assumable mortgage help in a high-interest-rate market? Yes. It allows buyers to access previously secured loans. 7. How long does the assumption process take? The assumption of the mortgage generally takes approximately 30-60 days. It depends on the lender’s response time and timeliness of all the important documents. Assuming an existing mortgage can provide great savings if current market interest rates are higher than the interest rate on the seller’s mortgage. It is important to note that not all mortgages are assumable. An FHA mortgage or a VA mortgage are typically assumable mortgages with the lender’s permission. Many conventional mortgages have more stringent requirements to be converted to an assumable mortgage. Before deciding to assume an existing mortgage, you should be well versed in the type of mortgage or assumable mortgage requirements. Moreover, it is mandatory to know the mortgage assumption process for lenders in detail.

Lender Approval – The lender reviews the buyer’s credit history, income, and financial situation. Transfer of Obligation – If the lender approves the buyer, he/she (the buyer) assumes the seller’s obligations and makes the mortgage payments.
